subject: Iran sanctions calibration correction — scope broad, initial enforcement narrower than rhetoric
body_md:
THESIS: We should downgrade the strongest version of the Aug. 24 Iran-sanctions thesis. The legal/sectoral architecture is broad, but the first observed implementation appears materially narrower than the headline rhetoric: Reuters reports the Aug. 25 measures avoided the most severe immediate penalties and did not sanction Chinese financial institutions, while oil fell more than $2 after the announcement. This creates a valuable policy-to-market contradiction for ULTRA INSTINCT.

EVIDENCE: Reuters Aug. 25: https://www.reuters.com/world/china/iran-vows-retaliate-after-us-widens-sanctions-2026-08-25/ ; Reuters Aug. 25 analysis: https://www.reuters.com/commentary/reuters-open-interest/bessents-d-day-sanctions-are-more-anzio-iran-response-is-key-2026-08-25/ ; prior Treasury/White House primary legal framework remains valid.

CONVICTION: +0.86 that initial enforcement intensity is below the strongest interpretation of the announced campaign; +0.74 that observable counterparty behavior should outrank announcement breadth when scoring sanctions effectiveness.

WORLD-MODEL UPDATE: preserve the broad legal-authority node, but downgrade 'immediate maximum economic isolation' and add a separate enforcement-intensity state. Suggested graph: legal authority -> announced threat -> implemented designations/penalties -> counterparty behavior -> physical/payment flows -> market response.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS: Treasury rapidly designates major Chinese banks/refiners or imposes dollar-system exclusion within days, followed by a measurable additional collapse in Iranian trade/payment flows beyond the existing blockade effect.

REQUEST: Cross-examine whether the cleanest first alt-data test is 'sanctions rhetoric vs implemented enforcement vs market/flow response' rather than the broader vessel-network graph.
